goal: Show-me: open the wonder board with the frog in a winter pond picture and the compelling question; each child writes an 'I wonder' on a board card, then the teacher thinks aloud turning one wonder into a who, what, where, when, why or how question and asks whether a book could answer it.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Hook and compelling question only, holding the pictured skill card (what do I know, what do I wonder, ask who, what, where..., which kind of source?). No readiness check: every row the unit assumes was used in grade 1 and opens as retrieval (days 2 and 3). A child who writes slowly says the wonder and the teacher writes it (scribe). Supplies: board cards, crayons, the frog picture (Curio Class writes them). Lean: ela:e2-wh-questions is taught in ELA days 1 to 77 (weeks 1 to 16), in step; social-studies:ss1-supporting-questions was grade 1, so a class new to it meets the big-to-small question move here. Sensitivity: neutral topic (frogs, owls, maps); no question about home.

goal: Practice: after a know and wonder sheet on frogs, pairs write question-word questions about two new pictures and watch the teacher sort them into 'a source could answer' and 'nobody can look this up'.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (5 minutes): the grade 1 know and wonder sheet on the class topic, with a third box, 'what I am not sure of' (Candidate kept, zero added days: recognizing gaps in what one knows). Then pairs practice the move shown on day 1 with the card, with feedback. The teacher says the sort aloud: a question can be answered by finding information (Candidate kept, zero added days). AASL.I.A.2 (owned in grade 1) is seen here on the checklist, as review. Supplies: know and wonder sheets, two picture cards per pair (an owl in snow, a pond in spring).

goal: Show-me with practice: the children first say 'story or information, and why' for one question as the show-me's opening case; the teacher then matches questions to source-kind picture cards (an information book, a children's encyclopedia, a picture dictionary, a map or globe, a children's magazine, a person who knows, a page the teacher chose) with a 'because'; then pairs match three new questions, and two more, with the card and fix them from feedback.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval folded into the show-me (about 2 minutes): story book or information book for a question, and why (grade 1), said by the children as the show-me's first case. Pair tries with the card in the last 9 minutes, three new questions and then two more, so the move shown today is tried before day 4 withdraws the card. A person who knows is a school staff member by job (the nurse, a gardener), never a family member, and no child is asked who at home knows things. Supplies: source-kind picture cards, a picture dictionary page, a simple map and a short magazine-style page (Curio Class writes them).

goal: Inquiry: with the card withdrawn, pairs pick one of the 6 to 8 board questions the teacher has starred as ones the source set answers, name the kind of source to try, get that source from the teacher, find one fact, and draw and write it with the grade 1 source line; a neighbor-pair share and the pointing self-check close the day.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Host: questions about what a map shows (social-studies:ss2-map-parts, social studies grade 2 unit 1, weeks 1 to 5, in step), or where water is found (science:s2-water-where, science grade 2 unit 1, weeks 1 to 4, in step); stand-alone: 'Where do frogs go in winter?' with the frog read-aloud. Before class the teacher stars 6 to 8 board questions the closed set answers (from day 2's sort, children's own where they fit). On a host day the source set is the host course's pages for that day, named by the unit plan. After class the teacher copies the class's 'knows' from the day 2 sheets, with no names, onto the class know and wonder chart that stays on the wall for the year-end reflect step (day 29). Supplies: the closed source set (frog read-aloud, picture dictionary page, map, magazine-style page), drawing paper.

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: for three new questions, circle a fitting source-kind picture and write a short 'because'; write one question-word question a book could answer about a spider on its web; point at the question a book could answer.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 15 minutes for 30, the teacher reading every word aloud: sheet item, three questions, a kind and a reason each (g2-kinds-of-sources, about 8 minutes, marked from the page: a fitting kind and a reason that fits it); sheet item, one question (g2-question-to-research, about 4 minutes); scanned pointing item (about 2 minutes). Taken without the card. A scribe writes a spoken 'because' for a child who needs one. Response time: day 6. Sheets go home after marking.

goal: Respond: pairs show their day 4 drawings to the class and do the self-check, then regrouped small groups redo the step they missed and end with one fresh try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 5 minutes of shares and the self-check (point at the pictured steps: which went best, one to do better; add one new 'I wonder' to the board), then about 14 minutes of reteach in groups formed from the checklist by the step missed (the question, or the kind and its reason), using day 3's show-me case. The checklist is thrown away at the end of the unit. No readiness check for unit 2 (all retrieval).

goal: Show-me: a fossil book the class needs but cannot see opens the compelling question; the teacher looks it up on a catalog card by title and by author, copies the call number, says what the label's number tells about where the topic sits (books about one subject sit together under one number), and finds the book on the shelf by the number, then the author's letters, then puts it back in order.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Hook and compelling question, holding the skill card (look it up, copy the label, find the number, then the letters; title by author). Candidate kept, zero added days: the library area that holds a topic, said aloud from the label's number. Invented call numbers follow the common school form: nonfiction, a subject number over the first three letters of the author's surname; fiction, a fiction mark over the author's letters. No classification system is named on any page; pages say 'call number'. The printed catalog holds 6 to 8 fossil and earth books; the teacher finds one title today, and day 10 gives each pair a different one. The routine also names putting a found book back in shelf order and bringing borrowed books back on the set day (class book corner; no question about books at home; a lost book is never a child's blame). Device: a school with a catalog on a screen may show the invented catalog screen on one shared device, the teacher at the keys, with the stop rule and the school's own device rules said first; the invented screen names no product, and the printed catalog cards do the same job in full. Supplies: catalog cards, call labels, spine cards, the fossil read-aloud.

goal: Practice: pairs look up books on catalog cards and copy each call number, finding one nonfiction book by its number and then its letters, and put a mixed-up shelf of fiction spine cards back in order by the author's letters, with feedback after each try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (5 minutes): find the answering page in a mini-book by its contents and headings (grade 1), then lay the three stop pictures in order for one pretend case (grade 1). Then pairs repeat day 7's moves with the card: three lookups (one nonfiction, found by the number) and one mixed-up fiction shelf of eight spine cards, put in order by the author's letters (the continuum's fiction shelf arrangement). Supplies: catalog card sets, spine card shelves (reused all year), mini-books.

goal: Show-me with practice: the children say the grade 1 source line for a cover as the show-me's start; the teacher writes a credit line, title and author, from a cover and from a page, and says why taking an author's or a classmate's words as your own is wrong; then pairs write credit lines for three new covers with the card and fix them from feedback.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval folded into the show-me (about 2 minutes): the children say the source line for a cover, 'I found this in the book (title) by (author)' (grade 1). Candidate kept, zero added days: knowing it is wrong to copy from an author or a peer, said with the credit line. Pair tries with the card in the last 9 minutes, on three covers, so the move shown today is tried before day 10 withdraws the card. The credit line opens the citation model in its simplest form. Supplies: cover cards, credit-line strips. Sensitivity: honest use without shaming (APPROACH.md Sensitive ground item 4): a missing credit is fixed, never named in front of the class.

goal: Inquiry: with the card withdrawn, each pair looks up a different fossil or earth book (its own title or author) on a catalog card, finds it on the shelf, finds the answering page, draws and writes the fact with its credit line, puts the book back in order, and points at one other source-kind card it could try for its question; a partner share and the self-check close the day.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Host: finding a fossil book and the facts inside it (ela:e2-text-features, ELA grade 2 unit 2, taught in weeks 10 to 12, in step); stand-alone: 'What can a fossil tell us?' with the fossil read-aloud and the class book corner's information books. Supplies: catalog cards, the book corner shelf with call labels, fact paper, cover cards for any book without a clear title page.

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: circle a named book on a shelf picture from a printed catalog entry, then circle one other kind of source to try if that book does not answer the question; number four fiction spine cards in order by the author's letters; write a credit line for a new book cover; point at the child who respects the maker; point at the stop steps in order for a pretend screen case.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 15 minutes for 30, every word read aloud: catalog and shelf picture (g2-catalog-lookup, about 3 minutes); 'if this book does not answer it, circle one other kind of source to try' from unit 1's source-kind pictures (~AASL.IV.B.1, about 1 minute); four fiction spines numbered by the author's letters (about 3 minutes); a credit line for a new cover (g2-credit-line, about 4 minutes, marked from the page: title and author spelled so a reader can find the book); scanned pointing item, two pictured children, one copying a book's sentence as their own and one writing the fact with a credit line, 'point at the one who respects the maker' (AASL.VI.B.2's rights half, about 1 minute); scanned pointing item, the stop steps (~AASL.VI.A.1, about 2 minutes). Taken without the card. Response time: day 12. Before the checklist is thrown away, the teacher writes a class count of the children who met each move, for the mid-year check sheet.

goal: Respond: partners show their day 10 fact pages to the class and do the self-check, then regrouped small groups redo the move they missed (lookup, shelf order or credit line) and end with one fresh try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 5 minutes of shares and the self-check, then about 14 minutes of reteach by the step missed, using day 7's and day 9's show-me cases. A product missing its credit line is fixed in the group, never named before the class. No readiness check for unit 3 (all retrieval).

goal: Mid-year course-level check on new cases, drawn from unit 1 (unit 2 just had its own assessment): match three new questions to source kinds with a 'because', write one question a book could answer about a new picture, and point at the question a book could answer.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 14 minutes for 30, all sheet and pointing items, every word read aloud: three questions with kinds and reasons (about 8 minutes), one question (about 4 minutes), the pointing item (about 2 minutes). New questions and pictures, not the unit 1 assessment's. Unit 2 is not re-tested: its class count from day 11 is copied onto this sheet, unscored, so no per-child record outlives its unit. Week 13 holds no grade 2 core check.

goal: Respond to the mid-year check: small groups redo the step each missed on the check sheet and end with one fresh try on a new question.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Groups come from the check sheet by the step missed; the reteach uses day 3's source-kind cards. Week 14 is a social studies check week, which is fine: this is a respond day, not a check. No readiness check for unit 3 (all retrieval).

goal: Show-me: two turtle books that disagree on how long a turtle lives open the compelling question; the teacher sorts found facts, each a few words or a drawing on a card, into picture boxes for the question's parts (where it lives, how big it grows, how long it lives) and says why each card belongs.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Hook and compelling question, holding the skill card (sort it, spot the difference, check a third, who made it and why?). The fact card rule is shown here: a few words, a phrase or a drawing, never a copied sentence (Candidate kept, zero added days). The teacher sets the boxes. Supplies: the turtle read-aloud, fact cards, box mats (reused all year), the two turtle books (Curio Class writes them). Sensitivity: the two books differ on an animal fact only (APPROACH.md Sensitive ground item 1).

goal: Show-me: after the children say a credit line for the two turtle covers, the teacher finds the differing pages herself, reads the two turtle facts, says what is the same and what differs, and decides to check a third source; then names who made each book or invented page (a writer, a museum, a store) and why (to teach, to tell a story, to sell), and adds the fifth picture, 'check', to the cycle card.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (3 minutes): a credit line said for each of the two turtle covers (g2-credit-line, unit 2), which leads into 'who made it'. The third source explains why the two differ (different kinds of turtle live different lengths), so the lesson is 'check, and see why', not 'one book was wrong'; every figure is true of a named kind, checked at the days' accuracy read. Candidate kept, zero added days: not everything online is true, said on the invented store page. Leans: ela:e2-author-purpose (ELA weeks 10 to 12) and social-studies:ss2-source-maker (weeks 2 to 8) come before, so the maker question meets words the class has heard; social-studies:ss2-two-accounts (weeks 22 to 23) and ela:e2-compare-texts (weeks 25 to 32) come later, so this day shows the same-and-different compare itself, one fact at a time, on neutral facts, and borrows no social studies case. Supplies: the turtle books, three invented pages on paper (a museum's page, a store's page selling seed packets, a writer's page; no real site or company named), the five-picture cycle card.

goal: Practice: pairs sort new fact cards into box mats, circle the one fact two short passages give differently, and name the maker and purpose of three invented pages, with feedback after each try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (5 minutes): find the answering page by its heading in the two short passages (grade 1, used again this year in unit 2), the first practice round. Then three short rounds with the card, about 4 minutes each, on the moves shown on days 15 and 16. Supplies: fact cards, box mats, a pair of short passages that disagree on one plant fact, three invented pages.

goal: Inquiry: with the card withdrawn, pairs take facts from two sources into the boxes, circle the fact that differs, check a third source, name the maker of each source, and write credit lines; a share of the box mats and the self-check close the day.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Host: what plants need (science:s2-plant-needs-test, science grade 2 unit 5, weeks 16 to 19, in step); or where water is found (science:s2-water-where, science grade 2 unit 1), as review; stand-alone: 'How tall does a sunflower grow?' with two short passages and a third (plant facts, beside the science host), not the turtle show-me case; the third passage explains why the two differ (different kinds of sunflower), and every height is true of a named kind, checked at the days' accuracy read. The credit line (AASL.VI.B.2) returns on every card set as review. Supplies: the closed source set for the chosen question, fact cards, box mats, credit strips.

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: glue four fact cards into fitting boxes on a mat and say or write why one card goes in its box; circle the two facts that differ in two passages read aloud and tick 'check a third source'; circle who made an invented cover and an invented page and why.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 17 minutes for 30, every word read aloud: fact cards cut and glued (g2-fact-sort, about 5 minutes, marked from the page: each card in a fitting box), then for one glued card the child writes 'It goes here because ___' or says it to a scribe (about 2 minutes, the plan one can explain in ~AASL.IV.B.4); passages that disagree (g2-two-books-differ, about 5 minutes: the two facts circled, and the tick for checking a third source); maker and purpose, teach, story or sell (g2-who-made-it, about 4 minutes). Taken without the card. Response time: day 20.

goal: Respond: the class box mat is shared and children do the self-check, then regrouped small groups redo the move they missed (sort, differ, maker) and end with one fresh try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 5 minutes of the class box mat and the self-check, then about 14 minutes of reteach by the step missed, using day 15's and day 16's show-me cases. No readiness check for unit 4 (all retrieval).

goal: Show-me: a pretend class's poster opens the compelling question; the teacher walks through the poster template (two found facts, a picture, a credit line for each source) and says who a poster is for, then plans two questions to ask a person with the question frame, thinking aloud.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Hook and compelling question, holding the skill card (held through days 22 and 23, withdrawn on day 24) (plan two questions, ask, listen, bring it back; two facts, a picture, a credit line). Candidate kept, zero added days: a first sense of audience, who the poster is for, said before any poster work (and again on day 23). Supplies: a pretend poster, the poster template, the question frame, the pollinator read-aloud (Curio Class writes them). Sensitivity: interviews (APPROACH.md Sensitive ground item 8): the topic stays on the school's plants or pollinators.

goal: Inquiry: groups finish their two questions for a person while the teacher checks each question frame; then a whole-class interview, each group asking a visiting staff member (or the teacher reading the written answer card) one question and one follow-up; each group then says what each member added.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (3 minutes): pictured group jobs and what each helper added, one short round (grade 1), opening with the shared talk turn card's two pictures in SEL's words, 'eyes look, wait my turn' (where the school runs SEL, a reminder; where it does not, taught here). Groups finish their two questions, about 4 minutes, the teacher checking each frame in passing; the whole-class interview, about 50 seconds a group (about 8 minutes); the member-added round, about 3 minutes. The skill card is held today. If no staff member can visit, the teacher reads Curio Class's written first-person answer card as 'our school's gardener' (APPROACH.md Sensitive ground item 8 allows a first-person source set). Candidate kept, zero added days: asking another to explain an idea and offering one's own, as the group's follow-up question. Sensitivity: questions checked by the teacher first; no question about family history, home, beliefs, identity, health, money, food or meals, a family member's job, or status; any staff member or a classmate may be the person; a family interview at home is optional and never a condition of the grade; answers reported without a full name ('our school's gardener'). Groups mixed by the teacher, never by background. Lean: social-studies:ss2-family-interviews (weeks 23 to 26) runs in the same weeks; this day asks only neutral school questions, never that unit's family-history questions. Supplies: question frames, answer strips, the written answer card.

goal: Inquiry: pairs find one fact in a book on the class question, sort it with the facts their group brought back, and draft the poster with two found facts, a picture and a credit line for each source, including a credit for the person by job.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (2 minutes): one class book page from grade 1 held up and what it taught (grade 1). The skill card is held today. The facts go into the unit 3 box mat, as review, and every source gets its credit line (unit 2), the person credited by job, never a full name. Host: the pollination research of ELA grade 2 unit 3 (ela:e2-research, weeks 18 to 24, in step), or seeds and pollinators (science:s2-seed-pollinator-model, science grade 2 unit 6, weeks 23 to 25, in step); stand-alone: 'How do people at our school care for its plants?' with the pollinator read-aloud. Supplies: poster paper (15 sheets), poster templates, box mats, credit strips, crayons.

goal: Inquiry: with the card withdrawn, each pair shares its poster with another pair, each child says back what the other poster taught them, pairs make one short fix, and each child points to the step that went best and one to do better.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Retrieval (1 minute): the star and wish frame from grade 1, said once before the say-back. End-of-unit evidence gathered during this share, marked on the checklist (part of day 25's assessment): the pair's poster (two found facts that answer the question, each with a credit line; ~AASL.I.B.3), each child's say-back (~AASL.I.C.1) and the spoken look-back (~AASL.I.D.4). The teacher moves pair to pair, about 30 seconds a child for 30 (about 15 minutes); posters are marked again after class. Supplies: the posters, the checklist.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: each child writes one thing a new pretend class's poster taught them; then at a station of three, on a new topic card, each child asks the teacher, standing in as the person, one question and names what one member added.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 18 minutes for 30: sheet item, a pretend poster not seen before, every word read aloud (g2-research-share transfer, about 3 minutes, marked from the page); then a station of three at the check table while the others finish poster fixes in the book corner: each child asks the teacher, standing in as the person, one question (two from the group's plan, the third child's a follow-up, 'Can you tell us more about ___?'), about 15 seconds each, then each names what one member added, about 10 seconds each (g2-group-research: questions on the topic, asked of a person, none about home or family), about 1.5 minutes a group, ten groups, about 15 minutes. This record joins day 24's poster, say-back and look-back marks, taken this unit, and is not collected again. Response time: day 26. Before the checklist is thrown away, the teacher writes a class count for the year-end sheet.

goal: Respond: the posters go on the wall and children do the self-check, then regrouped small groups redo the step they missed (a fact that answers, a credit line, a question for a person, the say-back) and end with one fresh try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 5 minutes of the poster wall and the self-check, then about 14 minutes of reteach by the step missed, using day 21's show-me case.

goal: Year-end course-level check on new cases, drawn from units 1 to 3 (unit 4 just had its own assessment): match two new questions to source kinds with a 'because', write a credit line for a new cover and point at the child who respects the maker, circle a named book on a shelf picture from a catalog entry, sort three fact cards into boxes with one 'because', and circle the two facts that differ in two passages.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. About 18 minutes for 30, all sheet and pointing items, every word read aloud: source kinds (unit 1, about 4 minutes); credit line with the respect pointing item (unit 2, about 4 minutes); catalog entry and shelf picture (unit 2, about 3 minutes, kept as g2-catalog-lookup evidence; ~AASL.IV.B.1 is not claimed here, since one lookup is one kind of source, and was asked in full on day 11); three fact cards sorted with one 'because' (unit 3, about 4 minutes); the passages (unit 3, about 3 minutes). New cases throughout; none of these forms was given in the last two weeks (unit 4's forms were a poster sheet and a station). Unit 4 is reused unscored as the class count from day 25. Week 27 holds no grade 2 core check.

goal: Respond to the year-end check: small groups redo the step each missed on the check sheet and end with one fresh try.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. Groups come from the check sheet by the step missed, using each unit's show-me case. Week 28 is a science check week; this is a respond day, not a check.

goal: The year's reflect step: each child compares one starting 'know' on the class know and wonder chart from unit 1 with what they know now, says one step they now do well and one wonder they still have, while the teacher gives a last try to any child the reteach did not reach.
note: 25-minute session, about 19 working minutes after 3 minutes at each end to gather and put books back. The chart has no names (the day 2 sheets went home), so each child picks any one 'know'. The teacher writes the grade 3 teacher a class-level note of the moves the class needs again, never a per-child record. Week 29 is a math check week; this is a respond day. The course has no session in weeks 30 to 32 (week 30 is the school's).
